approachQuestion.prompt:
A kit has n indivisible positive item weights. Decide whether some subset totals exactly S, using each item at most once.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= S < W <= 64; 1 <= weight[i] <= S. Return a Boolean.
Example: W=16, weights=[3,6,4], S=10 -> true, choosing 6 and 4. Edge case: weights=[3], S=6, W=8 -> false.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: A W-bit AND, OR, logical shift or bit test costs constant time. Shifts discard bits beyond W. The output Boolean and input are excluded from auxiliary storage.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Start B=1. For each weight a, compute B = B OR (B shifted left by a) using the previous B on the entire right-hand side. At the end test bit S.
options.feedback: Bit t records whether t is reachable. Shifting the previous states adds the current item once; positive weights mean discarded large sums can never return to S.

options.text: Use a Boolean array for sums 0 through S, updating sums downward for each item.
options.feedback: Descending updates correctly prevent reuse, but process and store each sum separately rather than packing the states in one word.

options.text: Use a Boolean array for sums 0 through S, updating sums upward in place for each item.
options.feedback: Ascending updates can reuse the same item: [3] and S=6 incorrectly marks 6 reachable after marking 3.

options.text: Sort a copy descending and take each weight if it fits the remaining target.
options.feedback: For [4,3,3] and S=6, greedy takes 4 and fails, although the two 3s form a valid subset.

feedback.reason: A set bit denotes a reachable sum.
details: Use one bit per achievable sum in a word initially containing only bit zero. For each weight, form the shifted old word before combining it with the old word. Test the target bit after all items; no reconstruction is requested.

A set bit denotes a reachable sum. Shift the old mask before OR so this item is used at most once. The one-word model is essential: if all target bits no longer fit one word, the same shift is not a constant-cost operation.

“Start B=1. For each weight a, compute B = B OR (B shifted left by a) using the previous B on the entire right-hand side. At the end test bit S.”: Bit t records whether t is reachable. Shifting the previous states adds the current item once; positive weights mean discarded large sums can never return to S.

“Use a Boolean array for sums 0 through S, updating sums downward for each item.”: Descending updates correctly prevent reuse, but process and store each sum separately rather than packing the states in one word.
“Use a Boolean array for sums 0 through S, updating sums upward in place for each item.”: Ascending updates can reuse the same item: [3] and S=6 incorrectly marks 6 reachable after marking 3.
“Sort a copy descending and take each weight if it fits the remaining target.”: For [4,3,3] and S=6, greedy takes 4 and fails, although the two 3s form a valid subset.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For shift-old-reachable-mask, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the item count; count W-bit word operations, with S < W.
constraints: A W-bit AND, OR, logical shift or bit test costs constant time. Shifts discard bits beyond W. The output Boolean and input are excluded from auxiliary storage.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: One old-mask shift and OR per item uses constant word storage.
details: One word shift and OR per item gives linear time; the current and shifted words use constant auxiliary words. There is no array of sums or call stack.
A W-bit AND, OR, logical shift or bit test costs constant time. Shifts discard bits beyond W. The output Boolean and input are excluded from auxiliary storage.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method does not retain a table or copy.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is looser than the bounded number of scans.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The input cannot be processed without scanning it in the worst case.
